'''''Rhododendron austrinum''''' is a species of flowering plant in the [[Ericaceae|heath family]] known by the common names '''Florida flame azalea''', '''honeysuckle azalea''', '''southern yellow azalea''', and '''orange azalea'''. It is native to the southern United States, where it can be found in [[Alabama]], [[Florida]], [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]], and [[Mississippi]].<ref name=tnc>[http://www.natureserve.org/explorer/servlet/NatureServe?searchName=Rhododendron+austrinum ''Rhododendron austrinum''.] The Nature Conservancy.</ref> It is also a common [[ornamental plant]].<ref name=cpc>[http://www.centerforplantconservation.org/Collection/CPC_ViewProfile.asp?CPCNum=3734 ''Rhododendron austrinum''.] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111026045132/http://www.centerforplantconservation.org/Collection/CPC_ViewProfile.asp?CPCNum=3734 |date=October 26, 2011 }} Center for Plant Conservation.</ref>

This species is a [[shrub]] growing up to 10 feet tall and 8 wide. It has [[deciduous]] oval leaves 2 to 4 inches long. It blooms profusely in large yellow or orange flowers which have a pleasant scent.<ref name=fla>[http://edis.ifas.ufl.edu/fp503 ''Rhododendron austrinum''.] University of Florida IFAS Extension.</ref> The [[stamen]]s protrude up to 2 inches from the flower's mouth. The funnel-shaped flowers are borne in clusters of up to fifteen.<ref name=mobot>[http://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/gardens-gardening/your-garden/plant-finder/plant-details/kc/c545/rhododendron-austrinum.aspx ''Rhododendron austrinum''.] Missouri Botanical Garden.</ref> The flowers come in before the new spring leaves emerge.<ref name=fla/>

The plant is a common garden species because of its showy, fragrant flowers in shades of yellow or cream to nearly red.<ref name=cpc/><ref name=nc>[http://www.ces.ncsu.edu/depts/hort/consumer/factsheets/shrubs/rhododendron_austrinum.html ''Rhododendron austrinum''.] North Carolina State University Horticultural Science.</ref> They attract [[hummingbird]]s and [[butterfly|butterflies]].<ref name=mobot/>

In the wild, the plant is a regional [[endemism|endemic]] occurring in and around the [[Florida Panhandle]]. It occupies moist and wet acidic substrates in ravines and other areas. It is threatened by the destruction of its habitat during conversion of the land to agriculture, [[silviculture]], and other uses.<ref name=tnc/>
